decision: Redesign the Meiku interface as a phone-only, QR-first app built on the shared ishiku design-system components.
rationale: The product owner approved the UI review (2026-10-31) and stated that Meiku is not used on desktop. Showing a QR code to someone in person is the core task, so the code, the share action and one-handed use come first.
consequences: Four swipeable share cards (Private, Business, PayPal, Bank) replace the three tabs with an inner PayPal/Bank switch.
QR codes use the scan-first 'soft' style: square single-colour modules with rounded finder patterns. Superseded in v0.4.1 by the 'fluid' style (REL-20261101).
Unlock shows the PIN pad directly when a PIN is set; six digits submit automatically, OK submits legacy 4–5 digit PINs.
The header has a settings button (meiku-client-vault profile); settings are grouped into Profile, Appearance, Vault and About with sub-sheets.
design-system/components.css and theme-controller.js are now loaded; css/meiku.css shrank from about 1,700 to about 630 lines of Meiku-specific styles.
app.js was split into app.js (controller), cards.js, settings.js, profile.js, dom.js and icons.js. Crypto, auth, store and QR payload logic are unchanged.
The service worker no longer triggers a page reload on activation, which previously cleared the setup form on the first visit.
No desktop layout is provided; wide screens keep the centred mobile column.
verification: Application command: 47 Python tests, crypto/store/auth/QR/profile Node suites, node --check for every module
Playwright walkthrough at 390x844 and 320x640 in light and dark mode: no console errors, no horizontal overflow at 320 px, setup input survives service worker activation, swipe updates the navigation
Accessibility audit of 14 screens and sheets: every visible control named, touch targets at least 44 px, inputs labelled, no duplicate ids
tests/e2e/migration.e2e.mjs (v0.2.x vault, legacy PIN and avatar migration, conflict, password change, import) passed against the new UI
